heuristics.statement: Our theory: the first blocks M0 are fresh uniform 512-bit strings; their chaining values CV1 = F_37(IV, M0) behave as independent uniform 256-bit values; in particular x = A_{-1} is uniform on 2^32 and independent of cb = C6 - A_{-2}, which is uniform on 2^32. Consequences used: each of the 170 classes passes the W7 test with probability p7 = |F7|/2^32 exactly, each variant of a passing class then passes F6 with probability p6 = |F6|/2^32 exactly, and given both, W0..W5 are uniform and independent of (W6, W7) (proof.md Lemma 5.1); hence the expected number of good pairs per first block is g = 599,760 p7 p6 = 636.680, the expected counts of the ledger, and the independence of distinct first blocks. The submitted executable samples exactly this law: with no seed argument its first blocks are 512 fresh uniform bits from the system CSPRNG per first block, not a stream expanded from one 32-byte seed (proof.md 8.2, `reports/experiments/r37-coins-209.py`); the seeded replay path is reproduction only and is not the distribution this probability is stated over.
heuristics.scope: The expected numbers of passing classes, good pairs, survivors and row-16 passes per first block; the expected operation count of the counted program; the law of the second-block words that defines q3; independence across first blocks (proof.md Section 10). Not the validity of any output: every output is verified with the target.

These are at most 2^23 real first blocks, not 2^55.8. P4 organizer executor observations under public seed hashsmash-public-seed-v1, no holdout nonce: 256 requested trials per experiment, two fresh executions with byte-identical stdout only. Internal counters are participant observations; the organizer independently checks returned-pair target events. These runs do not prove full-scale probabilities, H1-H7 or q3. P4 participant observations over 15000 blocks: W7=275, W6=3993, coW6=1267, w7_and_w6=22, w7_w6_pairs=60. No returned pairs. Runtime 6.75/6.35 s versus 20 s. heuristics.limitations: Premise (our theory), not a theorem: the filter rates are measured on at most 2^23 real first blocks and on the organizer's small samples, not at the 2^55.8 first blocks of the attack, and independence across first blocks is assumed, not tested. The class tests of one first block are strongly correlated (their c7 values are close), so per-first-block counts are overdispersed; only their expectations and the independence across first blocks are used. The class test uses the single word x, so H1 is also an assumption about that word of the digest of a 37-step compression. The unconditional class-pass counter's dispersion is measured in the package (proof.md Appendix P.3: pairwise co-pass 10.17 x p^2, design effect 26.0; the organizer sample's 4.04 passes per block is z = +3.66 under the counter's own variance, the 6,000-block control z = +0.14). Only the exact expectation enters the ledger.

In addition, the organizer experiment a0-sfs-r37 constructs and verifies full 37-step SFS collisions across 128 classes and all 8 pattern branches (63/64 on patterns 0..3 and 57/64 on R16x patterns 4..7 on our seeds ours-A-0..127; 13 of 13 returned pairs of trials 0..15 are found by the counted program), and the organizer experiment h3-ladder-r37 runs the row-16 stage of q3 on organizer seeds: 41 exact row-16 passes among 98,216 W6 passes (4.2e-4, two seed sets) against the 4.9e-4 (2^-11) per probed lane of the ledger (Appendix H). The four-pattern relaxation (exactly four feasible patterns, three verified further collisions) is ffbe30bb's; here the three collisions are re-checked against this package's cells. R16x is ours (each of its two conditions alone is necessary; a sweep of 30 further condition pairs found no further gain). Here the examined law is the studied law (every variant of every passing class, no weighting), so no hedge is added. The collision event after row 21 (Section 7.7): given rows 16..21, the outputs are equal iff E22[29] = 1, s1(W22') - s1(W22) = 0x4fff9f30 and dW26 = 0, with the uniform-model ratio 1275/512 = 2.4902 (4ec21bf9, Appendix D.2); the measured ratio is 2.4648 +- 0.0145 (Table 15 states), 2.4552 (ffbe30bb's states, three runs, the last preregistered) and 2.46455 (the attack's kept-fibre law, preregistered), every cell event also a collision event in every run, and the preregistered rule gives EXQ = min(2.482, 2.4443) = 2.482 (4ec21bf9, Appendices D.3, D.3b). With q3c one bit lower (q3 = 2^-72.4629 x 2.482) the claim would be 58.71038 (60.49449 under A_C = 2^60), with the four patterns alone (q3c = 2^-72.02) 58.29762 (60.38630 under A_C = 2^60), with the Table 15 value 2^-74.03 60.30330 (61.15945 under A_C = 2^60), and with the cell event of rows 22..36 instead of the collision event (EXQ = 1) 58.99371 (60.58264 under A_C = 2^60). These sensitivities use P4 prices and unchanged predicates with alternative q3 floors, rational 40-bit mantissas and ceil N_FB; the primary slack is retained or increased on the 10^-20 grid to preserve its Bernstein exponent, with time rounded upward to five decimals. Using the preregistered two-decimal floor 2^-71.47 gives 57.63320 (60.30327 under A_C = 2^60); the J2 bound alone 2^-71.4524 gives 57.88819 (60.29997 under A_C = 2^60), without replacing the declared min-block floor. P4 public-seed participant observations: a0-sfs returned/checked 121 pairs, detected 16/16; ladder row16=37/81608 W6 passes. Two byte-identical executor runs; no holdout. See the P4 executor observations section for runtimes and N/S/P/C/R.
heuristics.limitations: A Monte-Carlo and procedural premise, not a theorem: (1) its coverage rests on the approximate normality of the mean of 128 replicates (relative sd 0.1096 and 0.1143, about twice the Table 15 study's because few children survive the row-19 stage); row-22 survivors are heavily duplicated within a replicate; the row-22 stage draws (W6, W7) uniformly from F6 x F7, which is argued, not measured; depends on the reading of the '+' cells; (2) the offline preregistration timestamps/hashes (PREREG_q3M.txt, PREREG_q3R16x.txt) and contiguous seed lists (710000..710063, 720000..720127, 721000..721127, 740000..740127, 741000..741127) are participant-reported without an organizer holdout nonce, interim progress looks were taken while blocks ran (Appendices F.2 and G.2), and screening R16x against 30 other condition pairs before running J1 and J2 is not a multiplicity-adjusted holdout test, so the absence of material selection, optional-stopping, or multiple-testing bias is an explicit part of heuristic H2 rather than an externally certified guarantee; (3) no organizer experiment executes the end event of q3: rows 22..36 reach the digest only through a second-block chaining value that must be equal, which needs a reachable first block, that is the attack itself (a0-sfs-r37 returns semi-free-start pairs and no full collision of the target); the organizer-executed h3-ladder-r37 runs only the row-16 stage of q3 on organizer seeds; (4) EXQ = 2.482 is a Monte-Carlo bound from Block G (proof.md Appendix O: 1,024 fresh preregistered seeds 860000..861023 on this filing's characteristic, cells and 599,760-variant pool, 214,748,364,800 late proposals, R_pooled = 2.484920, LB_p = 2.482246, per-seed LB_s = 2.482320, declared EXQ = floor(1000 * min(LB_p, LB_s))/1000 = 2.482), not a theorem; the earlier runs of 4ec21bf9 (2.4648 +- 0.0145 on Table 15 states, 2.4552 on ffbe30bb's states, 2.46455 under its kept-fibre law, min bound 2.4331) are retained as sensitivities; no organizer experiment estimates the ratio. Premise (our theory): q3 is our computation, with the estimator, the preregistrations and the per-seed estimates printed in Appendices F and G. The count of four patterns is a solver enumeration (Bitwuzla; Z3 on smaller cases) for the published dense part with the signed cells of rows 14 and 15 kept (with rows 12..15 removed as well it admits 128 patterns); other dense parts were not explored, and our estimator does not use the solver. R16x has no solver enumeration: its value rests on the estimator, on a0-sfs-r37, and on our full-path test with rehashed collisions; patterns of rows 16..21 outside the program's cells (for example the E18 XOR pattern {24,23,16,15}) are not counted. A stated premise, not an established fact. Organizer reproduction route: the q3smc program and its constants are regenerable from the filed package and pinned by sha256 (reports/experiments/r37-g2fix-171.py: q3smc.c f0e3efc8, gen_consts.py 721d7949, q3consts_orig.h efd62db9, variants.bin b7671710, 4/4 MATCH), the study program is the filed program, and the 16,384-replicate re-measurement of Appendix N bounds the residual tail difference at +0.153% (0.0022 bit); the raw Block F/G stdout and per-seed estimates are printed in Appendices F and G.

heuristics.statement: Averaged over the trials t = (first block, variant, l) of a first block f weighted by their success probabilities, the expected number of other successful trials of the same first block given that t succeeds is at most 2^-9.4: sum_t Pr[A_t] E[X_f - 1 | A_t] <= 2^-9.4 E[X_f]. Equivalently: (a) the expected number of other l in L* succeeding with the same variant is at most 2^-11, and (b) for other good pairs t' of the same first block, Pr[t' succeeds | t succeeds, t' good] <= 2^35 Pr[t' succeeds | t' good].
heuristics.scope: The per-first-block Bonferroni bound Pr[X_f >= 1] >= (1 - 2^-10.4) E[X_f] (proof.md Section 10). The good pairs of a first block and their dependence structure are those of 7319bba; this filing changes the order in which they are processed, not the set.
heuristics.extrapolation: (a) 7319bba's replay of 19,620,436 distinct Step-3 successes of the SMC: rebuilding W0..W5 and testing the other 31 elements of L* through rows 14..36 gave 0 further successes (rule-of-three 95 percent bound 2^-22.65 per success; the accepted patterns raise the chance of passing rows 18 and 19 by about 4 and R16x the chance of the whole path by about 1.6, with four more l holding row 16, so about 2^-19.8, far below 2^-11; in that replay the other l fail at row 16 or 17; the collision event changes only rows 22..36, so (a), decided at rows 16 and 17, is unchanged). (b) Summing over all other trials t' = (f, a0', l') in the family uses the family average of Pr[t' succeeds | t' good], which is q3 <= 2^-71.38 x 2.4902 = 2^-70.0637 (H2, Section 7.7; no per-trial uniformity across (a0, l) is required), so the expected number of further successes among other good pairs is at most rho x N_good x 32 x q3 with N_good <= 599,760 (all variants of the family): 2^35 x 2^19.58 x 2^5 x 2^-70.0637 = 2^-10.4837, so delta <= 2^-11 + 2^-10.4837 = 2^-9.7189 < 2^-9.4; the measured factor at the row-16 level over 2^21 and 2^23 real first blocks is 0.98 and 1.00. The organizer experiment h3-cowpass-nonce counts the first blocks in which several variants of one class pass F6 together, and h3-ladder-r37 (Appendix H) counts, on organizer-seeded real first blocks, the pairs of distinct variants of one first block that both pass each level of the attack through the exact row-16 test, against the pairs expected if they passed independently: our replays (two seed sets) give the dependence factor 3.62 and 4.92 at the W6 filter (variants of one class share bits), 0.99 and 1.00 at historical aa0e8b6 LO12 and 0.95 and 0.94 at historical MID12 (P4 public-seed ladder R: W6=3.250842, FIRST13 (lo)=0.995964, SECOND11 (mid)=0.949225, exact row 16=1.048555; N/S/P/C and exact rational calculation are in the P4 executor observations section.), and 1.27 and 0.67 at the exact row-16 test (32 and 9 passes). This is the bound of the earlier filings on this family; the whole family G would give 2^-6.5 and is not used. P4 organizer executor observations under public seed hashsmash-public-seed-v1, no holdout nonce: 256 requested trials per experiment, two fresh executions with byte-identical stdout only. Internal counters are participant observations; the organizer independently checks returned-pair target events. These runs do not prove full-scale probabilities, H1-H7 or q3. P4 participant observations over 15000 blocks: W7=247, W6=4036, coW6=1264, w7_and_w6=27, w7_w6_pairs=82. No returned pairs. Runtime 6.70/6.54 s versus 20 s. P4 public-seed ladder R: W6=3.250842, FIRST13 (lo)=0.995964, SECOND11 (mid)=0.949225, exact row 16=1.048555; N/S/P/C and exact rational calculation are in the P4 executor observations section. FIRST pass rate 15131/81608=0.185410744045 versus 1513/8192=0.1846923828125 under the uniform-address model of the 13/11 tables the ladder ran against (R37P38 resplits the probe top-first 15/9, whose first stage passes on 2207/32768 indices, proof.md 6.2); SECOND conditional rate 307/15131=0.020289471945 versus the approximately 0.0205 reference. There are 37 row-16 passes among 81608 W6 passes. Eight returned generic 4-bit witnesses pass the organizer mask event; they are not full collisions. Runtime 4.37/4.19 s versus 20 s. Current P4 ladder (N,S,P,C,R): W6=(839808,81608,171761468,5595314112,3.250841661); FIRST13/lo=(81608,15131,5880837,171761468,0.995963919); SECOND11/mid=(15131,307,2298,5880837,0.949225494); row16=(307,37,35,2298,1.048555259). R=P/[C(S/N)^2], summed once across trials.
heuristics.limitations: Premise (our theory): rows 17..36 are not reachable by any organizer experiment of 20 s; for them rho = 2^35 over the measured factor (0.67 to 1.27 through row 16 on organizer seeds; 0.98 and 1.00 over 2^21 and 2^23 real first blocks) is the stated allowance. Rows >= 17 of distinct good pairs cannot be measured jointly within one first block; the premise leaves a margin of 2^35 over the measured row-16 factor, and the margin over the number of examined pairs is thin (delta <= 2^-9.72 against 2^-9.4). The replay samples are correlated through SMC resampling. A stated premise, not an established fact.

heuristics.statement: The published characteristic, its two-bit conditions, the SFS pair's inner values S and L* are used as advice. Their construction is charged A_S = 2707315195888 = 2^41.3 (the Step-1 SAT solve, reported by the paper at 2^41.3, and the completion of a Step-1 solution to the SFS pair, 25 ms) and calibrated A_C = 2^48 (the unpublished characteristic search, > 169 times the 593,858 solver CPU-seconds = 2^40.61 units measured for the predecessor 35-step search in 6eeefb64; sensitivity at A_C = 2^56, 2^60, 2^64 is reported in proof.md Section 12); all development computation at DEV = 2^40. The variant family, the 170 class descriptors (below 2^13 bytes), the lists, the filter sets, L* and the tables are recomputed in the preprocessing (2^39 operations bound, itemised in proof.md Section 14.2).
heuristics.scope: The preprocessing part of the ledger (2^48.01938) and the advice (below 2^13 bytes).
heuristics.extrapolation: proof.md Section 11.2. A_S: the paper's reported Step-1 cost itself (2^41.3), not a multiple of it; the completion of a Step-1 solution to a full 37-step semi-free-start pair is reproduced in this package in about 25 milliseconds per pair (organizer experiment a0-sfs-r37). A_C: at the CPU-second price calibrated in the accepted filing 6eeefb64 (2^21.427 units at C = 2644 per solver CPU-second), A_C = 2^48 units is 2^26.57 solver CPU-seconds (~3.17 core-years), > 169 times (2^7.39x) the 593,858 solver CPU-seconds (2^40.61 units) that filing charged as a measured complete re-run of the predecessor 35-step search; we also report sensitivity across the full unamortized allowance spectrum: A_C = 2^56 gives time_log2 = 57.68010, A_C = 2^60 gives 60.18623, and A_C = 2^64 gives 64.01238. P4 organizer executor observations under public seed hashsmash-public-seed-v1, no holdout nonce: 256 requested trials per experiment, two fresh executions with byte-identical stdout only. Internal counters are participant observations; the organizer independently checks returned-pair target events. These runs do not prove full-scale probabilities, H1-H7 or q3. P4 participant observations: 118 returned pairs and checks_passed=118; detected_by_counted_program=16 for all 16 returned trials 0..15. Organizer checked all 256 trial records (121 returned pairs), with 0 full-target collisions; SFS validity remains an internal participant check. Runtime 7.65/7.48 s versus 20 s.
heuristics.limitations: The 37-step characteristic search time is unpublished; A_C = 2^48 is calibrated with a 2^7.39x factor above the accepted measurement of the predecessor 35-step search (593,858 solver CPU-seconds = 2^40.61 units in 6eeefb64), not a direct measurement of the paper's search. A_C = 2^56 would give time_log2 = 57.68010, A_C = 2^60 would give 60.18623, and A_C = 2^64 would give 64.01238.

heuristics.statement: Under collision-frontier-v5 a word-RAM program of 256-bit primitives in which every executed load, store, logic operation, shift, addition, comparison, branch and jump is one primitive is charged by the primitives it executes. The W7 class test (106 primitives for all 170 classes) and the W6 test of a batch of 256 reps (181 to 301 primitives, and 11 to 28 for each subtraction run) are straight-line plane programs whose counts do not depend on the data, produced by a plane algebra in which static constants fold and complemented planes carry an inversion flag at no cost, and in which a NOT is paid when an AND or OR meets unequal flags; two batches are processed together bit by bit with at most 20 live planes each (64 registers, no spill). Each rep word of the packed table holds its 64-bit entry in all four lanes (proof.md 9.6c; same 2,048 words and 65,536 bytes), so member placement executes no spread. The per-rep charges are MEMBER_CHARGE = (5, 4, 2, 3) for m = 1, 2, 4, 8 members, itemised in 9.6c; the group word is consumed from its register with no store, as in the inherited m = 1 discipline. The lane-placed delta words are charged explicitly: DELTA_CLASS = 18 per passing class and DELTA_RUN = 5 per run. selftest checks the member identity, not the counts, on 110,592 members. The group of four members is 28 primitives (28 packed-u lines; no word-level address mask is executed, and the group counter is batched into the per-rep update), the first probe stage 12 primitives per four lanes (every lane shifts by 64k+9, so lane 0 pays a shift too) plus seven per nonzero FIRST word (2207/32768), the residual exact row-16 test 13, and the zero-base scan_table at word address 0 prices CLS_LANE = 5, SCAN_LANE = 5 and SURV_LANE = 6, with the scalar and control items of proof.md Section 9. All tables (including the 16,384-byte prefilter table of proof.md 9.6e), the code (78,826 inherited bytes plus a 1,024-byte allowance) and the constants occupy 1,035,912 bytes = 2^19.982470, below 2^20 bytes. The 170 classes are base | s for s in the four kept lists 0, 1, 5 and 6 (computed, checked for all 599,760 variants); a list is the union of 2^|B| translates of its reps by the cube B of free bits {0, 2, 3, 7}, {0, 2, 3} or {0}, and F6(W6x) does not depend on a cube bit s_b when q_b = 1 or on s_0 when CB3_0 = 1 (Lemma 8.2: proved from the constants of S and checked), which the program uses to run only the main combination and subtract the constants of the other 2^|Q0| - 1 combinations that matter. The seven-lane first-block batch's 174 separately executed non-compression operations (48 message-generation/packing and 126 extraction/hand-off per seven blocks) are charged in addition to the seven one-unit compressions, at ceil(N_FB/7) batches (F-COST-1; proof.md 9.11).
heuristics.scope: The class-test, W6, scan, gather, group, probe and survivor terms of the ledger (essentially all of the 11880.95 data-dependent operations per first block), the fixed terms, the memory figure and the preprocessing bound (2^39 operations).
heuristics.extrapolation: The program is experiments/lowm.py (the plane programs assert their counts at every execution; process_cv counts every scalar item where it executes; the realized operation count of every category equals its closed formula on 20,000 simulated first blocks). It is exact against the scalar definitions: every lane of every class-test plane and every pass plane equals the F7 or F6 test of its definition (34,000 and 33,570 lanes in selftest, and every lane of every processed class in a0-online-r37), the sets of good pairs (all members, after the expansion of the reps) equal the brute-force sets, the address u equals W0 + s0(W1) from the step equations, the exact row-16 test equals the enumeration of 2,097,152 pairs on all 32 l (Appendix A) and the generic row check on random and near-miss values, and the table stage never rejects a member. These reported simulations are inherited aa0e8b6 evidence; P4 organizer execution completed; The changed table and residual predicates are independently exhaustively checked. P4 organizer executor observations under public seed hashsmash-public-seed-v1, no holdout nonce: 256 requested trials per experiment, two fresh executions with byte-identical stdout only. Internal counters are participant observations; the organizer independently checks returned-pair target events. These runs do not prove full-scale probabilities, H1-H7 or q3. P4 participant observations: 512 unconditional first blocks, 2070 class passes; 52 selected first blocks, 24 processed classes, 7152 good pairs, 25 survivors. class_lane_mismatches, pass_lane_mismatches, goodset_mismatches, address_mismatches, row16_mismatches and cell_mismatches each total 0. Five returned pairs, 0 organizer full-target collisions. Runtime 1.92/1.93 s versus 20 s.
heuristics.limitations: No organizer ruling is cited for the plane algebra (static constants and inversion flags are compile-time facts of the text; the W6 programs have 32 to 84 inversion flips that cost nothing because XORs absorb them and AND/OR of equally flagged planes use De Morgan; pricing every one of them as a NOT would give 58.0603, or 60.3339 under A_C = 2^60) or for the register argument, which is a count of live planes, not a register allocation. The code size is a bound (at most 8192 primitives of at most 8 bytes). Branch pricing follows the earlier filings (a branch on a register is one primitive). The ceiling of the group count and the survivor scan are charged at their worst case (below 0.2 percent of the data-dependent work). The compression clause is applied as a floor (rulings ba65804c and f044761e F1): each first-block selected-target compression is charged as one unit (SB_FB = 2644), not the 384 primitives per first block the seven-lane batch executes; the claim is 57.21778 (the R37P40g row at the same charge: 57.24415). The scan and padding rates are empirical premises with the same standing as H1-H4 (declared in H6-SCAN-PADDING-RATES): each filed ROW_FIX is the 99th percentile of a 2,000-resample block bootstrap over first blocks of the shipped generator (design effect 25.6; two independent 2,000-block runs move the nl = 256 charge by -6.7%), the filed values are 1.152-1.159x the per-run means and 2.8-3.7% above the measured block bounds, and PAD_RATE is the one-sided 99% Poisson upper bound on the measured pad counter over 5,000 real first blocks (charged against both the extra group word and the padded body, 0.00388 bit; vmax_fb keeps its maximum); the receipts and organizer corroboration are reproduced in proof.md Appendices P and Q.

heuristics.statement: The 0.39 floor is reached with named constants: mu_req = -ln(0.61 - Pcap - 2^-60)/(1 - 2^-10.4) = 0.494663010083979 at assumed Pcap = 9/25000000 = 3.6e-07, rounded up to 0.49466302. N_FB = 30821554876811406 and the achieved mean is at least mu_req; Appendix C gives the exact fraction and the floor 0.39000000604429280 > 0.39. Earlier historical revisions used different constants.
heuristics.extrapolation: The floor includes the Bernstein cap-failure bound Pcap, the repeated-first-block allowance 2^-60, and the H3 discount 1 - 2^-10.4. At slack 1/15000 the reported cap bound is approximately 3.579311e-07, below the assumed 3.6e-07. Appendix C recomputes the requirement, achieved mean and floor with 60-digit decimals. The current proof is a draft while inherited statements and supporting evidence are reconciled.
heuristics.limitations: The 0.39 floor is the organizer's success requirement; the reported margin is approximately 7.08e-10 and depends on the stated precision. The cap bound requires H1 and the maximum per-block work bound. Historical ledger passages and the remaining cost and probability evidence require review before this draft is ready.

heuristics.statement: Every phase this submission runs executes with peak resident memory no greater than the declared 1,035,912 bytes = 2^19.982470, below 2^20: the 2^29-candidate family discovery is streamed against a 65,536-byte key table and 2,080 bytes of counters, the list/plane/table build uses at most 2^17 bytes of scratch from the not-yet-initialised scan-table region and never duplicates a final table, and the advice (the published characteristic, its conditions, the Step-1 solution and the SFS pair) is stored data of at most 2^13 bytes (proof.md Section 14.3). No search is omitted: the program runs no solver.
heuristics.scope: Peak resident memory of the submitted program at every phase, together with the retained advice. The work of those phases is charged separately in time under A_S = 2^41.3 and A_C = 2^48; memory has no scalar contribution under collision-frontier-v5 and is reported and reviewed as a metric.
heuristics.extrapolation: The key table is bounded by the 520 distinct c7 values and at most eight masks each; a pass that exceeds 4,096 entries is repeated over the same stream under a different key partition, and four passes (4 x 2^36 = 2^38) are charged inside PRE = 2^39 (which since R37P40h also covers the prefilter table build, below 2^36.6, proof.md 14.2 (v)), so the streaming argument costs nothing outside the preprocessing budget already charged. FIRST, SECOND, the scan table and its successor table (8192 words each) are disjoint regions of the same 1,035,912 bytes and are written in place (proof.md 14.1-14.3). The advice is the cited work's published Tables 15-17, stored rather than recomputed, and its construction is charged in time at A_S = 2^41.3 and A_C = 2^48, 2^48.02 units together, more than 169 times the measured complete re-run of the predecessor search.
heuristics.limitations: The published characteristic's own search time was never reported by the cited work; A_C = 2^48 is a calibrated allowance more than 169 times the accepted measurement of the predecessor 35-step search (sensitivities at A_C = 2^56, 2^60 and 2^64 are stated in proof.md 11.2), so the time bound for that step is an allowance rather than a measurement. Memory has no scalar contribution under collision-frontier-v5; it is a reported metric and this statement is what supports it.

heuristics.scope: The ROW_FIX scan charges, the PAD_RATE residual-padding charge, and the row-16 stage of the per-first-block price (proof.md Sections 9.6 and 8.1/6.2).
heuristics.statement: The expected scan rate of a 64-bit row (the ROW_FIX charges at nl = 256/194/176/216/225 and the 170-lane class plane) and the residual-padding rate PAD_RATE are empirical premises of the per-first-block price, declared here explicitly: each filed ROW_FIX is the 99th percentile of a 2,000-resample bootstrap over first blocks of the shipped generator (block-level, design effect 25.6, two independent 2,000-block runs moving the nl = 256 charge by -6.7%), the filed values are 1.152-1.159x the per-run means and 2.8-3.7% above the measured block bounds, and PAD_RATE is the one-sided 99% Poisson upper bound on the measured pad counter over 5,000 real first blocks (charged against both the extra group word and the padded body, 0.00388 bit; vmax_fb keeps its maximum). They are measured generator regularities under the public seed, charged conservatively; they are not organizer-executed in the filed headline: an organizer-executed corroboration of the same instrument (manifest experiment `h6-orgstats-r37`, organizer-side 99% bounds re-priced to 57.05523 against 56.99456 at this revision's cells and the former 384 charge (at most 57.28905 against the filed 57.21778 at the one-unit charge; the bound was computed on the R37P40k cells and the folds only lower it) (57.06265 against 57.00229 on the R37P40g row; 57.10920 against 57.05080 on the R37P39 row); 57.16006 against 57.10307 on the base 3c71035b row) and the declared analytic replacement — the structural worst case with every rate at its extreme (all rows set at the true ROW_MAX ceiling of proof.md 9.6c, every block padded), priced at 57.16021 (57.15946 on the base row with its lower ROW_MAX) — are carried in proof.md Appendix Q, bounding the row's reliance on these premises at 0.1094 bits.
heuristics.limitations: Rates are participant-measured on public-seed generator output with no organizer holdout; the 99% bootstrap/Poisson bounds are the declared confidence discipline, and the row moves by only 0.00388 bit if the padding premise is replaced by its worst case. The measurement receipts are carried in the package (proof.md Appendix P: the ROW_FIX block-bootstrap and the PAD_RATE Poisson receipts, verbatim).
heuristics.extrapolation: The extrapolation is the like-for-like discipline of proof.md 9.6: measured block-level generator rates are charged at their 99% bootstrap/Poisson upper bounds, and the residual row moves by at most 0.00388 bit under the worst-case padding replacement (proof.md 8.1/6.2). Public-seed participant measurements, no organizer holdout: declared as a premise, sensitivity-bounded, and small against the 2,644-unit reference.
